title: A Level 45 Blacksmith Just Killed A Level 140 Boss . . . (Episode 6)
caption:
In Overgeared episode 6, Khan offers Grid his forge, a ghost gives him a legendary job quest, and he fights a level 140 frost orc chieftain.
He survives with a sidekick he cannot shake. Follow for episode 7!

#overgeared #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have kept Hu-Roy as your sidekick after all that? Why?

segments.say: A level 45 blacksmith and his clingy sidekick just killed a level 140 *boss*.
To see how it got here, go back to Takumi, who is still sixty million yen in *debt*.
He just forged a legendary sword, and his stats shot through the *roof*.
But stats do not pay off a loan, so he decides to lock in and make real *money*.
At the forge, old Khan catches him hammering away with a pile of broken *tools*.
Khan loses it. A blacksmith's hammer is his very *life*.
So he fetches a hammer that boosts rare crafting by ten *percent*.
Grid raises it like treasure, furious Khan never mentioned it *sooner*.
Khan just laughs. Grid has made him laugh more than anyone in years.
Then the old man gets quiet. It is the anniversary of his son's death, and he wants company at the *grave*.
His son Oliver was a great blacksmith who died ten years ago, before he could take over the *forge*.
Grid always thought NPCs were just code, but this one looks pretty *real*.
Khan tells his son that Grid saved the forge and made him quit *drinking*.
Then he drops the big one. He wants Grid to take over the *forge*.
Grid is stunned. He tells Oliver his father is now his best *friend*.
Then the graveyard starts to glow, and a row of ghosts rises from the *ground*.
They are Khan's ancestors, and they came to thank Grid for caring about their *descendant*.
One of them says he was awestruck by the legendary blacksmith Pagma a hundred and thirty years *ago*.
He painted Pagma's sword dance on a cliff in Kasong Canyon, and Grid gets a legendary job *quest*.
Grid cannot believe it. After all that grinding, he finally has the first step of his legendary *class*.
The ghost asks for one thing in return. Take care of my *father*.
Grid promises. Then Khan wakes up, thinking he just dozed off at the *grave*.
Meanwhile, the Yatan Church crushed Earl Stime's army, and the North's best knight barely *survived*.
Quests go up across the continent, and the whole world waits to see who will *fight*.
A dark mage in the church brags that he has finally passed the limits of his *class*.
Grid does not care about any of it. He wants to clear his first job *quest*.
Then his sidekick Hu-Roy turns up, fully healed and begging to serve his *master*.
Grid tells him to back off. Hu-Roy kneels in the street and will not *quit*.
That man needs a *hobby*.
So Grid ignores him. But Kasong Canyon is full of level 160 monsters, and he is only level *forty-five*.
Khan says he needs a sylphid scale, the scale of a tiny wind *fairy*.
Grid uses his legendary skill to design a new armor around it, right on the *spot*.
The scales drop from frost orcs in the north, so he sews himself a fur *set* and walks off.
Khan watches him go, worried. The drop rate is less than one *percent*.
Grid hikes into orc territory, and a whole horde jumps *him*.
He is outnumbered. His health bar turns red, and even his immortality skill will not *save* him.
Then a title he earned by saving an old man kicks in and gives him a new *skill*.
Grid starts swinging, and frost orcs drop like flies. He levels up *all night*.
Meanwhile, Hu-Roy trudges through the snow, swearing he will find his *master*.
After days of grinding, Grid has killed eighty orcs for three scales, but his level has nearly *doubled*.
Then Hu-Roy finally finds him and starts kneeling again. Grid wants to *strangle* him.
That is when the snow shakes. A frost orc chieftain spawns, level one hundred and *forty*.
Hu-Roy reveals that standing near Grid boosts his stats by thirty percent, and Grid lets him join the *party*.
Grid goes wild with his blacksmith's wrath skill and wipes out the whole orc *horde*.
Now it is just the chieftain, and they hit him with double *justice*.
But one swing sends Hu-Roy flying. He is out *cold*.
Grid is alone against a brick house of a boss, and every sane instinct says *run*.
So he stays. The Legendary One title makes him immune to every status effect, and his fear just *vanishes*.
All his life, Takumi has been the supporting character. Not here. Main character *energy*.
He tells the boss it is going to have one hell of a time taking him *down*.
Then Hu-Roy wakes up, bleeding, and tries to get back into the *fight*.
He swears that whatever the boss throws at him, he will *block it*.
Then the chieftain throws fire bottles, and Grid freaks out, because orcs cannot use stat boost *items*.
Hu-Roy has a plan, a technique called Sacrifice for Justice. He tells Grid to leave the rest to *him*.
It does not work, but it drops the boss's defense, and Hu-Roy pays for it with his *life*.
Hu-Roy perishes, and for once Grid says *thanks*.
Then his cooldown ends, and Unyielding Justice is ready *again*.
He swings it, and the Frost Orc Chieftain finally goes *down*.
Grid shouts that they did it. The first step of his legendary quest is done, and the war with the Yatan Church is *coming*. Follow for episode 7!
